jobs.description:
Built's Mission:  Connect and simplify doing business in real estate.

Built is the AI-powered platform transforming the way real estate is financed, developed, and managed. Purpose-built for real estate and construction, Built began by fixing construction draw management for lenders and has grown into a comprehensive operating system addressing some of the industry’s most complex challenges. Today, Built is a partner to more than 350 lenders, over 80,000 borrowers and owners, and thousands of contractors, powering 86,000 active projects valued at more than $300 billion. Learn more at  getbuilt.com .
__________________________

Campaign Marketing Manager

About Built

Built is transforming the real estate industry with modern SaaS solutions that help those financing, building, and managing projects work more efficiently. Our platform supports the full construction ecosystem, including Owners, Developers, General Contractors, lenders, subcontractors, and suppliers.

About the role

Built is hiring a Campaign Marketing Manager to drive demand, adoption, and growth among Owners, Developers, and General Contractors. This role will turn the business unit’s highest-priority customer challenges and commercial bets into clear marketing strategies and creative, integrated campaigns.

You will translate business priorities, customer insight, and Built’s central messaging into cohesive campaign narratives. You will own the campaign strategy for this audience, identify the moments and customer needs that matter most, set the creative direction and content brief, and orchestrate execution with Growth, GTM Engineering, Events and ABM, Communications, and Enablement.

This role is ideal for a marketer who combines strong judgment about audience intent with an instinct for great creative. You know how to make a complex B2B story feel relevant, urgent, and easy to act on. You are comfortable using data to improve campaigns quickly and care as much about product adoption and expansion as you do about pipeline.

What you’ll do

Own integrated campaign strategy

- Translate business strategy, customer needs, and growth goals into a focused campaign roadmap for the business unit.

- Identify the highest-value audiences, use cases, buying moments, and growth opportunities.

- Build campaign briefs that define the audience, objective, customer insight, message, creative direction, channel plan, offer, and success measures.

- Set campaign success measures before launch, including qualified pipeline, engagement, eligible-account adoption, and expansion indicators.

Develop creative campaigns that create and capture demand

- Create integrated campaign concepts that make Built’s value proposition compelling to Owners, Developers, and General Contractors.

- Develop messaging and content direction that speaks to customer pain points, desired outcomes, and in-market intent.

- Unify paid, owned, field, sales, and customer touchpoints into one cohesive campaign motion.

- Partner with Creative, Content, Growth, GTM Engineering, Events and ABM, and Communications to bring campaigns to market.

Drive demand, adoption, and commercial results

- Partner with Sales leaders to align priority segments, accounts, and campaign goals to the business unit’s pipeline plan.

- Work with GTM Engineers to build audiences, activate campaigns, test hypotheses, and optimize performance.

- Work with Enablement to ensure Sales, Account Management, Customer Success, and Implementation teams can carry the campaign story into customer conversations and adoption motions.

- Test and improve performance across audience, message, creative, offer, and channel mix. Use results to improve future campaign strategy and investment.

Bring customer insight into the work

- Stay close to the market, target accounts, customer conversations, and competitive landscape.

- Turn customer insight, sales feedback, and intent signals into sharper campaign choices and creative ideas.

- Partner with Product and central marketing teams to understand upcoming releases and identify the right moments to bring them into market-facing campaigns.

What you’ll bring

- 3+ years of experience in B2B demand generation, integrated campaign marketing, growth marketing, or related roles.

- Demonstrated ability to build and execute multi-channel campaigns that drive measurable business results.

- Strong creative instincts and an ability to turn customer insight into clear campaign ideas, messaging, and content direction.

- Comfort using performance data to evaluate campaign results, diagnose what is working, and recommend clear next steps.

- Experience collaborating across Sales, Account Management, Customer Success, Product, Growth, and creative teams.

- Strong project management skills and the ability to bring multiple contributors together around a clear plan.

- Experience in construction, real estate, financial services, or vertical SaaS is a plus.

What success looks like

Within the first six months, you will have:

- Established a clear campaign roadmap tied to the business unit’s biggest growth opportunities.

- Launched integrated campaigns with a consistent story across marketing and customer-facing teams.

- Built a repeatable process for using audience intent, customer insight, and performance data to improve campaigns.

- Created measurable contributions to pipeline, product adoption, and expansion goals.

Built’s salary range for this position is $70,000 - $95,000 USD per year. The pay range is designed to accommodate upward mobility in the role, therefore it encompasses the full span of proficiency levels for this role and we believe that the midpoint of the range is competitive in the market. Salary is just one component of Built's total compensation package for employees; your total rewards package at Built will include equity, market-current medical, dental and vision coverage, an unlimited PTO policy, and other benefits.
__________________________

Travel Requirement: Employees who are not based in the Nashville area are required to travel to our Nashville office at least twice per year for company gatherings, such as Connect Week. Additional travel to Nashville may be required based on your role and business needs.

Perks:

- The rare opportunity to radically disrupt a $1.5T industry

- Competitive benefits including: uncapped vacation [US ONLY], medical, dental & vision insurance

- Robust compensation package, including equity in the form of stock options

- Learning Grant program to support ongoing professional development

- 401k with match and expedited vesting [US ONLY]

jobs.title: Marketplace Partnerships Lead
jobs.location: Nashville, TN or  New York City
jobs.description:
Built's Mission:  Connect and simplify doing business in real estate.

Built is the AI-powered platform transforming the way real estate is financed, developed, and managed. Purpose-built for real estate and construction, Built began by fixing construction draw management for lenders and has grown into a comprehensive operating system addressing some of the industry’s most complex challenges. Today, Built is a partner to more than 350 lenders, over 80,000 borrowers and owners, and thousands of contractors, powering 86,000 active projects valued at more than $300 billion. Learn more at  getbuilt.com .
__________________________

About The Role

Built Technologies is the AI-first platform for construction and real estate finance, managing over $300 billion in annual capital for more than 340 lenders — including 45 of the top 100 U.S. banks. Built's Marketplace connects the capital that funds construction with the services that get projects built — inspection firms, appraisers, environmental consultants, title and closing providers, materials suppliers, and specialty diligence vendors — creating a single embedded layer where lenders, owners, and general contractors can procure, manage, and pay for project services without leaving the platform.

This role is responsible for growing and strengthening the supply side of Built's vendor network. Most of Built's vendor relationships today have grown inbound and passively, through lender referrals, rather than through a deliberate program. This role changes that: going outbound to existing and prospective vendor partners, building the commercial frameworks that make those relationships pay off for both sides, and negotiating and closing the deals directly.

The core of this role today is supply-side partnerships — diligence and procurement categories such as inspections, appraisal, environmental, and title/closing to start, followed by labor & materials procurement — supply chain and trade partnerships that enable GCs, owners, and developers to source and purchase through Built-facilitated channels. Beyond that core, there are two directions the role could grow into over time, if the supply-side work proves out and the business need materializes:

- Demand-side & channel partnerships — referral, reseller, and co-sell relationships that extend Built's reach into new customer segments and adjacencies.

- Data & technology partnerships —integrations with third-party platforms, data providers, and technology vendors that expand the Marketplace's value to end users.

This is a 1-to-N role. You are building the partnership function, the playbook, and the pipeline from scratch — not inheriting a mature program. You will define the ideal partner profile for each category, build the commercial frameworks (revenue share, referral fees, SaaS bundles, procurement margin), negotiate and close the first cohort of partnerships, and design the operating model that lets the network scale without scaling headcount linearly.What You'll Do

Design the Partnership Operating Model

- Build the end-to-end partner lifecycle: sourcing, qualification, contracting, onboarding, performance management, and renewal/expansion.

- Define partner tiers, SLAs, and quality standards that let Built guarantee service levels to lender, owner, and GC customers.

- Create the operational infrastructure — onboarding playbooks, performance tracking, escalation paths — needed to run a growing vendor network without scaling headcount linearly.

Grow and Strengthen the Supply-Side Network

- Source, evaluate, negotiate, and close partnerships with inspection firms, appraisal companies, title and closing providers, environmental consultants, and other diligence vendors that serve lenders and owners.

- Run a systematic outbound program across Built's existing vendor network where you’ve identified opportunities for improvement and/or service or pricing irregularities.

- Continuously identify, evaluate, and prioritize the next wave of service categories to bring into the Marketplace catalog. Use a structured framework — e.g., segmenting services by how frequently they're ordered and how standardized their pricing is — to decide where a partnerships-led, negotiated approach beats a simple self-service vendor-onboarding motion.

Cross-Functional Coordination & Boundaries

- Partner with Legal and Compliance to develop partnership agreement templates and vendor qualification criteria appropriate to financial services.

- Work with Product and Engineering to define the platform capabilities a scaled vendor network needs — partner APIs, marketplace UX, order management.

What You'll Bring

- 6+ years of experience in supply-side partnerships, vendor management, procurement, or business development — ideally in B2B SaaS, fintech, construction technology, or real estate services.

- Proven track record of building a partnership program or vendor network from scratch (0-to-1), not just managing an existing book of partners.

- Deep understanding of marketplace or platform economics — two-sided network effects, take rates, procurement margin, and partner unit economics.

- Experience negotiating and structuring commercial agreements: negotiated rates, volume-based pricing, referral fees, and RFP-driven bespoke pricing.

- Strong operational instincts — you build the process, the playbook, and the systems alongside the relationships.

- Ability to context-switch fluidly between strategic planning, commercial negotiation, and hands-on operational execution.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence executives and align cross-functional stakeholders.

- Comfort with data and analytics — you can size a partner opportunity, model the economics, and defend the numbers.

What Success Looks Like at Six Months

- You have defined the partnership strategy and ideal partner profiles for all of Built’s existing service offerings, with a prioritized pipeline of target partners.

- A repeatable partnership operating model is in place — contracting templates, onboarding playbooks, SLA frameworks, and performance tracking — ready to scale beyond the initial cohort.

- You have closed and onboarded the first cohort of vendor or channel partners, with at least one category generating live transactions on the Built platform.

- You have a prioritized, evidence-based roadmap for the next wave of supply-side categories (environmental and beyond), including your recommended sequencing and rationale.

AI & Technology Expectations

- Leverage AI tools to enhance the productivity, quality, and speed of your work.

- Use AI to support drafting, analysis, summarization, and problem-solving across your role.

- Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort through automation and AI.

- Apply AI to sharpen decision-making and strengthen strategic insights.

- Share effective AI use cases and best practices with your team.

The pay range is designed to accommodate upward mobility in the role, therefore it encompasses the full span of proficiency levels for this role and we believe that the midpoint of the range is competitive in the market. Salary is just one component of Built's total compensation package for employees; your total rewards package at Built will include equity, market-current medical, dental and vision coverage, an unlimited PTO policy, and other benefits.

jobs.description:
Built's Mission:  Connect and simplify doing business in real estate.

Built is the AI-powered platform transforming the way real estate is financed, developed, and managed. Senior Manager, Client Success (Lender)

About The Role

Built Technologies is transforming how capital moves through construction and real estate finance — one of the largest, most complex sectors in the economy. Our platform connects lenders, including many of the top U.S. banks, with the owners, developers, and general contractors they finance. When a draw is approved, a builder can pay subcontractors. When a compliance document clears, a project moves forward. The work we do here is not abstract — it has a direct and material impact on how capital flows and how real estate gets built.

Built's Client Success team drives the retention, adoption, and value realization that make our customer relationships durable and growing — and the Senior Manager of Client Success leads that function at a broader scope. In this role, you will oversee strategic CSMs and managers, drive the strategic direction of the entire client success function, and partner with executive leadership on how the organization scales with Built's growth. At this level, you manage managers or a large team, operate with high autonomy, and connect your function's work directly to Built's net revenue retention, expansion revenue, and market reputation. You build high-performing organizations, develop leaders, and represent client success as a strategic driver of Built's business.

Our Guiding Principles

- Be Bold. We pursue the biggest problems in our industry, challenge assumptions others take for granted, and take calculated risks to get there. We don't hide behind consensus or committees. Playing it safe is just failing slowly.

- Help Customers Win. We learn our customers' businesses deeply — how they think, how they deploy capital, what keeps them up at night. We treat their capital like our own. We ship leverage, not features. And we measure ourselves by customer results, not our intentions.

- Move with Urgency & Purpose. We bias toward delivery over perfection, remove friction from our own paths, and communicate in real time. Momentum compounds — and we build it every day.

- Own the Outcome. We own outcomes, not just tasks. We hold a high Say:Do ratio and take responsibility from idea through impact. When something breaks, we fix it — we don't wait to be asked.

- Never Satisfied. We raise the bar continuously. We stay curious, hold exacting standards, debate hard, and hold our opinions loosely when the evidence shifts. Excellence is a habit, not an event.

What You'll Do

- Lead Client Success team and Managers of Client Success — establish organizational structure, strategic priorities, and performance accountability across a broader span of people and client relationships.

- Develop and implement organization-wide client success strategy, playbooks, and operating methodologies that drive consistent retention and expansion outcomes across all client segments.

- Hire, develop, and mentor CS managers and senior leaders — build a culture of accountability, client obsession, and continuous improvement that attracts and retains top CS talent.

- Set performance expectations and metrics for the client success function — monitor NRR, retention, adoption, and expansion results, and implement improvements that drive consistent commercial outcomes.

- Partner with Sales, Implementation, Product, and Finance to align client success strategy with company objectives and ensure Built delivers a seamless, high-value client experience across the full lifecycle.

- Lead strategic client relationships at the executive level for Built's most important accounts — serve as the senior CS voice in executive client conversations and maintain high-level presence in the portfolio.

- Drive innovation in client success approaches, tooling, and engagement models — continuously improve how the team identifies, develops, and captures expansion opportunities at scale.

- Develop annual forecasts and business plans for customer retention and expansion targets; represent the function's performance and strategy clearly to executive leadership.

- Champion AI and automation adoption across the function — build the systems and expectations that let the team manage more clients more effectively without proportional growth in headcount.

What You'll Bring

- 8–12+ years of experience in client success, customer success, or strategic account management, with 3–5+ years leading multi-level teams or managing a client success function in a high-growth SaaS or fintech environment.

- A proven organizational builder — you've developed CS managers and senior ICs, built strong team cultures, and created conditions where client success professionals do the best work of their careers.

- Deep expertise in client success strategy — scalable engagement models, health scoring, expansion playbooks, and the commercial levers that drive strong NRR in a SaaS business.

- A demonstrated ability to partner with executive leadership on strategy — translating company growth objectives into CS operating plans and connecting team performance to revenue outcomes.

- Executive presence and communication skills to represent the CS function at the senior leadership level — advocating for your team, your methodology, and the organizational investment required to retain and grow Built's customer base.

- Deep familiarity with lending institutions, draw management, compliance workflows, commercial real estate finance, or commercial banking — enough to lead the most important executive conversations and represent Built credibly at the highest client levels.

- Comfort with complexity and the pace of a high-growth company where client mix, team capacity, and organizational priorities shift continuously.

What Success Looks Like at Six Months

- The Client Success organization is delivering at scale — NRR is strong and improving, teams are retaining and expanding their portfolios, and Built's customers experience CS as a differentiator.

- At least one CS manager or senior IC on your team has meaningfully grown in scope, capability, or commercial performance under your leadership within the first two quarters.

- Client success methodology and tooling have evolved under your ownership — the function is more scalable, more consistent, and better equipped to serve Built's most complex clients.

- Executive leadership and cross-functional partners view you as a strategic partner on customer revenue — you're consulted on portfolio strategy, commercial planning, and client lifecycle design.

- The Client Success function has a strong identity, high-performance culture, and a reputation within Built as the team that drives the retention and expansion that fuel long-term growth.

AI & Technology Expectations

- Leverage AI tools to enhance the productivity, quality, and speed of your work.

- Use AI to support drafting, analysis, summarization, and problem-solving across your role.

- Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort through automation and AI.

- Apply AI to sharpen decision-making and strengthen strategic insights.

- Share effective AI use cases and best practices with your team.
